## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### z386: An Open-Source 80386 Built Around Original Microcode
URL: https://nand2mario.github.io/posts/2026/z386/
First complete open-source recreation of Intel's 80386 using disassembled original microcode
This pairs with the 80386 microcode disassembly project to create something unprecedented: a fully transparent implementation of a historically critical CPU. The implications extend beyond retrocomputing hobbyists—this provides a reference architecture for hardware verification, security research, and educational purposes. Open silicon movements continue gaining momentum as chip complexity drives demand for auditable designs.

### .NET (OK, C#) Finally Gets Union Types
URL: https://andrewlock.net/exploring-the-dotnet-11-preview-2-dotnet-gets-union-types/
Microsoft adds discriminated unions to C# in .NET 11 Preview 2, closing a major gap with functional languages
This is a decade-overdue feature that eliminates entire categories of null-reference bugs and clunky pattern-matching workarounds. Enterprise .NET shops—still a massive installed base—get a meaningful productivity upgrade. Watch for this to accelerate F#-style domain modeling adoption across the Microsoft ecosystem.

### Wayland Compositor Implemented as a Mod in Minecraft
URL: https://modrinth.com/project/9yAfrPwH
A functional Linux display server running inside Minecraft demonstrates Wayland's architectural flexibility
Beyond the absurdity, this proves Wayland's protocol is clean enough to implement in hostile environments. It's a flex that doubles as documentation of the API surface. For embedded and specialized display use cases, Wayland's composability continues to win converts from X11.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### SolarSquare in Talks to Raise Up to $60M as India's Rooftop Solar Market Draws Major VC Interest
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/23/solarsquare-in-talks-to-raise-up-to-60m-as-indias-rooftop-solar-market-draws-major-vc-interest/
Indian rooftop solar installer targeting $500M valuation amid surging distributed generation demand
India's residential solar penetration sits below 5%, versus 15%+ in mature markets. SolarSquare is riding government subsidy programs and plummeting panel costs. The valuation implies roughly 8x revenue multiple if they're at $60M ARR—aggressive but defensible given TAM expansion. Watch for consolidation plays as larger energy players seek distribution networks.

### Nuclear Startup Deep Fission Says It's Going Public, Again, and I Have Questions
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/23/nuclear-startup-deep-fission-says-its-going-public-again-and-i-have-questions/
Deep borehole reactor company attempts second IPO run seeking $157M amid skeptical investor scrutiny
The "again" is the red flag. Deep geothermal nuclear concepts face geological uncertainty, regulatory timelines measured in decades, and capital intensity that makes traditional nuclear look lean. The $157M target suggests they're struggling to close private rounds. Distressed tech-adjacent energy plays deserve careful due diligence on milestone achievability.

### Peec More Than Doubled Annualized Revenue to $10M
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/23/peec-one-of-berlins-rising-startups-more-than-doubled-annualized-revenue-in-months-to-10m-sources-say/
Berlin startup tracking brand presence in AI search results hits inflection point as enterprises scramble for visibility metrics
This is the "SEO for LLMs" play, and the revenue trajectory suggests real enterprise pull. As Google cedes search share to AI assistants, marketing budgets need new attribution tools. Peec is early to a category that could become mandatory spend. European SaaS showing signs of life.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Reverse Engineering Circuitry in a Spacelab Computer from 1980
URL: https://www.righto.com/2026/05/reverse-engineering-spacelab-computer.html
Ken Shirriff's latest teardown reveals radiation-hardened design choices in NASA's orbital lab hardware
The Spacelab computer ran ESA's science missions through the Shuttle era. This analysis exposes how 1970s engineers achieved fault tolerance without modern ECC or redundancy—techniques increasingly relevant as terrestrial chip geometries shrink to radiation-sensitive scales. Aerospace heritage systems remain gold mines for reliability engineering insights.

### The Architecture of BerkeleyDB
URL: https://aosabook.org/en/v1/bdb.html
Canonical reference on the embedded database that powered everything from LDAP to Bitcoin's early versions
BerkeleyDB's MVCC implementation and log-structured storage influenced SQLite, LMDB, and countless key-value stores. Oracle's acquisition and licensing changes pushed alternatives, but the architecture remains a masterclass in transaction processing at constrained scales. Required reading for anyone evaluating embedded database tradeoffs.

### Software Engineering at the Tipping Point
URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2n41YjR5QfU
Video analysis of how AI coding tools are restructuring development workflows and team compositions
The "vibecoding" tag signals this addresses the cultural shift, not just tooling. As Copilot and Claude penetrate enterprise dev shops, the leverage gap between senior and junior engineers widens. Teams are flattening faster than HR org charts reflect. Hiring models built on pyramid structures face reckoning.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The week's pattern is clear: infrastructure is getting re-examined at every layer. Open-source CPU implementations, language-level type system upgrades, and AI search attribution tools all point toward a maturing industry questioning inherited assumptions. Meanwhile, energy tech continues its bifurcation—solar scales predictably in emerging markets while nuclear ventures struggle for credibility. The talent market signal to watch: enterprises are buying tools that make smaller teams more capable, not tools that require larger teams to operate.
